agent: unitdemand (OpenHOI3: what a new game's and a loaded game's first screen show of the units' demand and the reinforcement and upgrade needs)
question: What writes CCountry unit_demand, reinforcement_cost and upgrade_cost, and whether anything in CInGameIdler::Enter does - so whether the first screen's three slider needs are the second day's or an estimate

addresses.name: RunCountryDailyPass_CarriageDemand
addresses.comment: **The carriage of supplies out to a country's provinces, added to what its units asked for.** In RunCountryDailyPass, straight after RunCountryDailyPass_WaitingUnitsDrawSupplies (and the free of the list at +0xD20), the loop VA 0x4DB311..0x4DB3FA walks the country's ControlledProvinces (CCountry +0xD00, each node {province id, ?, next}), looks each id up in g_CurrentGameState +0xB8C, and where **units_count (CMapProvince +0x2C0) > 0**, or else where the naval base's level_max (+0x300 -> CProvinceBuilding +0x20) > 0 **and** today's throughput of supplies (+0x1F8 -> CGoodsPool +0x8) is 0, adds supply_depot_hops (+0x50) x 1000 x SupplyLoss(province) / 1000 - the hops times the loss, thousandths, the divide by __alldiv - to unit_demand.supplies (CCountry +0xA48). Nothing else is added; fuel is untouched. So the supply share's need (CDistributeSupply::GetNeeded reads +0xA48) carries the network's carriage to every held province with anybody's unit in it, and to an idle harbour. No gate of its own: it runs wherever the country's unit block runs. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-laterstart.md, section 18.
addresses.evidence: Read on the listing (disasm.py 0x4DB29D 0x1B1): mov edi,[ebx+0xd00]; per node edx=[node], eax=[gs+0xb8c][edx*4]; cmp [eax+0x2c0],0 / jg add; mov ecx,[eax+0x300]; cmp [ecx+0x20],0 / jle skip; mov ecx,[eax+0x1f8]; cmp [ecx+8],0 / jne skip; add: esi=[eax+0x50]*0x3E8, lea ecx,[ebp-0x2c]; push ecx; call 0x49DE80 (SupplyLoss, province@EAX); imul [out]; __alldiv by 0x3E8; add [ebx+0xa48],eax. Found by a linear sweep of .text for every store with displacement 0xA40..0xA5C: the only CCountry writers of unit_demand are CCountry::CCountry, CCountry_Reset, CCountry::ClearDailyPools, CUnit::ConsumeSuppliesAndFuel (six adds) and this one. Built in OpenHOI3 (CSupplyCarriage); no save keeps unit_demand, so it is set beside nothing directly - with it the 1936 new game's written `distribution` (the AI's shares, which read the supply need) is the start save's for 7 more countries (67 written otherwise where 74). Shown wrong by a province with neither a unit nor a naval base adding to unit_demand, or by the add landing on another field than +0xA48.

addresses.name: CInGameIdler_Enter_RunDistributions
addresses.revises: the comment: 'reinforcement does nothing' - it moves nothing, but it and the upgrade share zero and count again their needs here; and what that means for a new game's and a loaded game's first screen
addresses.comment: **Entering a game runs every country's ten shares with nothing to share out.** In CInGameIdler::Enter's per-country pass after the information caches (VA 0x65C170 on; FINDINGS-savegame.md A.5's "the 6+4 distributions"), for each country of the list, after 0x4E21E0, 0x4E39C0 and 0x4DDD80: the loop at VA 0x65C1B0..0x65C1E5 calls **slot 0 of each of the six IC shares** (CCountry +0x5F4, `cmp edi, 0x18`) with (&out, an __int64 available of **0**, flag **1**), and the loop at VA 0x65C1E9..0x65C21E the same on the four leadership shares (+0x5E4, `cmp edi, 0x10`); then, where +0x640 is above 0, slot 4 of the fourth leadership share (CDistributeResearch::ShareAmongProjects) at VA 0x65C237; then, for a country owning a province (+0xCF8) that is not REB and whose strategy is neither initialized (+0x48C+0x14) nor static (+0x15), CAIStrategy::Rebuild at VA 0x65C282. Nothing tests loaded_from_save here, so a loaded game runs it too. What the shares do with nothing: **the upgrade share moves every doctrine a brigade is behind in a level** (CDistributeUpgrade::Distribute reads no flag and a doctrine costs nothing); reinforcement moves nothing (it acts only while its budget is above 0); production reads the flag and skips the AddProgress(0) a line would get with an empty pool (0x51A213). **But reinforcement and upgrade both zero and count again their needs** - reinforcement_cost (+0xA98), reinforcement_manpower_needed (+0xA9C), reinforcement_manpower_used (+0xAA0, left at 0) and upgrade_cost (+0xAA4) - which they do whether or not anything is spent. In a new game the block at VA 0x65C7F0 (the two days) comes after this, and each day's shares count them again, so **a new game's first screen shows the second day's needs** and a loaded game's this run's; neither is saved. unit_demand is written by no share and by nothing in Enter (RunCountryDailyPass_CarriageDemand). Of the ten bodies only CDistributeConsumerGoods (0x518DE8) and CDistributeProduction read the flag; what consumer goods does with it, and what espionage and research do with nothing, was not followed. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-laterstart.md, sections 10 and 18.
addresses.evidence: The calls and arguments are the existing record's, re-read on the listing (disasm.py 0x65C120 0x140): every country of the vector, no gate before the two loops. The counters: CDistributeReinforcement::Distribute zeroes +0xA98 at VA 0x51BBF6 and adds to it at 0x51C5FC outside the budget test, CDistributeUpgrade::Distribute zeroes +0xAA4 at 0x51CF4C and adds at 0x51D4E1 (the sweep of .text for displacements 0xA98 and 0xAA4; their other CCountry writers are CCountry::CCountry and CCountry_Reset only - the hits in CInGameIdler::CInGameIdler, its destructor and CInGameIdler_RefreshMap are CInGameIdler's own fields). The order against the two days is FINDINGS-savegame.md A.5's table. Shown wrong by a write to +0xA98 or +0xAA4 after VA 0x65C7F0 in Enter, which the sweep found none of.

struct_fields.name: unit_demand
struct_fields.revises: the comment only: every writer named, the carriage among them, and that nothing in entering a game writes it
struct_fields.comment: What the units drawing on this country asked for today, before any shortfall - supplies accumulate at +0xA48 and fuel at +0xA4C on every path through CUnit::ConsumeSuppliesAndFuel, including the one where the pool cannot pay. Distinct from CCountry::usage (+0x98C), which only gets what was actually handed over. **Every writer** (revised 2026-11-15): CCountry::CCountry and CCountry_Reset set it to nought, CCountry::ClearDailyPools zeroes it at the head of each day before the supply pass, CUnit::ConsumeSuppliesAndFuel adds each unit's ask (the units waiting to be placed included, RunCountryDailyPass_WaitingUnitsDrawSupplies), and RunCountryDailyPass_CarriageDemand adds the carriage - each held province with a unit in it, or an idle harbour, its supply_depot_hops times SupplyLoss - to the supplies. **Nothing in CInGameIdler::Enter writes it**, and it is not saved: a new game's first screen shows the second day's, a loaded game's nought until the first midnight. CDistributeSupply::GetNeeded makes the supply share's need from +0xA48. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-laterstart.md, section 18.
struct_fields.evidence: A linear sweep of .text (capstone, every memory operand with displacement 0xA40..0xA5C on a non-stack base): CCountry stores only at the constructor (0x4C9338..), CCountry_Reset (0x4D3B48.., from the zero global 0x1A87818), ClearDailyPools (0x4F295E..), ConsumeSuppliesAndFuel (0x5BBAB1, 0x5BBB9E, 0x5BBFC6, 0x5BC091, 0x5BC1E0, 0x5BC29F) and 0x4DB3F2 in RunCountryDailyPass; the other hits are other classes' fields (0x69Dxxx, 0x72Exxx, CCombatView). The save has no key for it (no 'demand' in Germany1936_01_01_00). Shown wrong by an indexed store (pool + 8 + good * 4) into it from Enter, which a displacement sweep could miss.

struct_fields.name: reinforcement_cost
struct_fields.revises: the comment only: its writers, and when the first screen's figure is made
struct_fields.comment: what reinforcement currently costs; the spare IC calculation subtracts it from what the reinforcement slider allocates. Thousandths of IC; CDistributeReinforcement::GetNeeded is it. **Written** (2026-11-15) by CDistributeReinforcement::Distribute alone in play - zeroed at VA 0x51BBF6 and every brigade's day of IC added at 0x51C5FC whether or not the budget allows anything - and set to nought by CCountry::CCountry and CCountry_Reset. Not saved: entering a game runs the share with nothing to spend (CInGameIdler_Enter_RunDistributions), so a loaded game's first screen shows that run's need, and a new game's the second day's, its days coming after. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-laterstart.md, section 18.
struct_fields.evidence: The displacement sweep for 0xA98: CCountry stores at 0x4C93C2 (constructor), 0x4D4612 (CCountry_Reset, esi zero), 0x51BBF6 and 0x51C5FC (CDistributeReinforcement::Distribute); loads at CCountry::GetSpareICIn (0x4F4C22) and CDistributeReinforcement's GetNeeded, tooltip and Distribute. The 0x647BD5 and 0x649B6B stores are CInGameIdler's constructor and destructor on their own object. Name and type unchanged.

struct_fields.name: upgrade_cost
struct_fields.revises: the comment only: its writers, and when the first screen's figure is made
struct_fields.comment: what upgrading currently costs; the spare IC calculation subtracts it from what the upgrade slider allocates. Thousandths of IC; CDistributeUpgrade::GetNeeded is it. **Written** (2026-11-15) by CDistributeUpgrade::Distribute alone in play - zeroed at VA 0x51CF4C and every outstanding level's daily cost added at 0x51D4E1, spent or not - and set to nought by CCountry::CCountry and CCountry_Reset. Not saved: entering a game runs the share with nothing to spend (CInGameIdler_Enter_RunDistributions), so a loaded game's first screen shows that run's need, and a new game's the second day's, its days coming after. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-laterstart.md, section 18.
struct_fields.evidence: The displacement sweep for 0xAA4: CCountry stores at 0x4C93D4 (constructor), 0x4D4624 (CCountry_Reset), 0x51CF4C and 0x51D4E1 (CDistributeUpgrade::Distribute); loads at CCountry::GetSpareICIn (0x4F4C5F) and CDistributeUpgrade's other slots. 0x647BE1, 0x649B40 and 0x651D16 are CInGameIdler's own field (constructor, destructor, CInGameIdler_RefreshMap). Name and type unchanged.

struct_fields.name: supply_depot_hops
struct_fields.revises: the comment only: the reader at 0xDB3CC is read - the carriage added to unit_demand
struct_fields.comment: the plain hop count to the depot, as against the weighted cost at +0x4C. Zeroed for every province by CSupply::RebuildSupplyNetwork and set to the parent's value plus one each time CSupply::SpreadFromDepot relaxes a neighbour. CSupply::DailySupplyPass never reads it; its other reader, VA 0x4DB3CC, is RunCountryDailyPass_CarriageDemand, which adds it times SupplyLoss to the controller's unit_demand.supplies for a held province with a unit in it or an idle harbour (FINDINGS-laterstart.md, section 18).
struct_fields.evidence: The 0x4DB3CC load (mov esi,[eax+0x50]; imul esi,esi,0x3E8) on the listing, eax the province from the controlled-provinces walk. Name and type unchanged.
